summary.text: A 74-year-old woman with a past medical history of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine was brought to the emergency department after being found unconscious at home. She had altered mental status, hypothermia (93 degrees Fahrenheit) and hypertension (185/97 mm Hg). Admission laboratory tests showed leukocytosis, serum sodium 163 mmol/L, creatinine 3.47 mg/dL, TSH 168 mIU/mL and free T4 0.33 ng/dL, and her ECG showed ST elevations in the anterior leads.

She had a myxedema coma with an ST-elevation MI. Emergent cardiac catheterization showed no plaque, thrombus, spasm or dissection, and transthoracic echocardiography showed apical ballooning with a hyperkinetic base and a moderately reduced ejection fraction, confirming Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

She was managed conservatively with beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors and aspirin, and a head CT was unremarkable. In the intensive care unit she continued intravenous levothyroxine and hydrocortisone but remained confused, aphasic and minimally responsive, and brain MRI showed two acute left caudate infarcts and white matter disease.

CT angiography showed left M2 intracranial stenosis, and transesophageal echocardiography showed an aortic plaque without other cardiac embolic sources. A loop recorder was recommended to investigate possible atrial fibrillation. Venous ultrasound showed a left posterior tibial deep vein thrombosis; she was placed on apixaban and discharged in a stable state with advice to follow up.

ambiguities.text: The ST-elevation MI is stated as a finding before catheterization ("Thus, she had a myxedema coma with an ST-elevation MI"); the later echocardiogram is said to confirm Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, but the source never says the MI was ruled out, revised or misdiagnosed, nor calls it a differential. Verification status stays unknown; it is not refuted.

ambiguities.text: The Discussion states a hedged mechanism by which myxedema coma could have induced Takotsubo cardiomyopathy in this patient; it is a possibility, not a documented cause, and no fact was recorded.
